title: Git Workflow — Branching, Merging, and Pull Requests
description: Practice the full Git workflow: init, branch, commit, merge, push, and create a Pull Request on GitHub
objective: Students will initialize a Git repo, create feature branches, make commits with meaningful messages, merge branches, push to GitHub, and create a Pull Request

steps.title: Initialize a Git Repository
steps.instructions:
Create a project folder and initialize Git:
```bash
mkdir my-project
cd my-project
git init
```

Create initial files:
```bash
echo "# My Project" > README.md
echo "__pycache__/" > .gitignore
echo ".env" >> .gitignore
echo "node_modules/" >> .gitignore
```

Make your first commit:
```bash
git add README.md .gitignore
git commit -m "Initial commit: add README and .gitignore"
```

Check status and log:
```bash
git status
git log --oneline
```

You should see 1 commit in the log.

steps.title: Create a Feature Branch
steps.instructions:
Create and switch to a new branch: ```bash git branch feature-homepage git checkout feature-homepage ``` (Shortcut: `git checkout -b feature-homepage` does both) Now create an `index.html` file: ```html My Project

Welcome to My Project

This is the homepage.

``` Commit it: ```bash git add index.html git commit -m "Add homepage with basic HTML structure" ``` Add a stylesheet and commit: ```bash mkdir css ``` Create `css/style.css` with basic styles. ```bash git add css/style.css git commit -m "Add stylesheet with body and heading styles" ``` Check the branch difference: ```bash git log --oneline --all --graph ``` You should see `feature-homepage` is 2 commits ahead of `main`.

steps.title: Merge and Handle Conflicts
steps.instructions:
Switch back to main and merge:
```bash
git checkout main
git merge feature-homepage
```

This should merge cleanly. Now let's simulate a conflict:

```bash
# Create another branch
git checkout -b feature-about
```

Add an `about.html` file and commit.

Now switch to main and make a conflicting change:
```bash
git checkout main
```

Edit `README.md` on main:
```markdown
# My Project
A demo project for learning Git.
```
Commit it.

Now edit `README.md` differently on feature-about:
```bash
git checkout feature-about
```
Change `README.md` to:
```markdown
# My Project
This project demonstrates Git branching and merging.
```
Commit it.

Merge into main:
```bash
git checkout main
git merge feature-about
```

If there's a conflict, Git will show:
```
<<<<<<< HEAD
A demo project for learning Git.
=======
This project demonstrates Git branching and merging.
>>>>>>> feature-about
```

Resolve by keeping what you want, then:
```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "Merge feature-about: resolve README conflict"
```

steps.title: Push to GitHub and Create Pull Request
steps.instructions:
Create a new repository on **github.com** (no README, no .gitignore).

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/my-project.git
git push -u origin main
```

Refresh your GitHub repo page — all files should be there.

Now create a feature branch for a PR:
```bash
git checkout -b feature-contact
```

Add a `contact.html` file, commit, and push:
```bash
git add contact.html
git commit -m "Add contact page with form"
git push -u origin feature-contact
```

On GitHub:
1. You'll see a "Compare & pull request" button — click it
2. Title: "Add contact page"
3. Description: What you added and why
4. Click "Create Pull Request"
5. Review the changes in the "Files changed" tab
6. Click "Merge pull request" → "Confirm merge"

Pull the merged changes locally:
```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
```

steps.title: Review Git History and Clean Up
steps.instructions:
Review your complete Git history:
```bash
# View commit graph
git log --oneline --all --graph

# See which files changed in each commit
git log --oneline --stat

# See the diff for a specific commit
git show HEAD

# List all branches (local and remote)
git branch -a

# Delete merged feature branches (cleanup)
git branch -d feature-homepage
git branch -d feature-about
git branch -d feature-contact
```

Verify on GitHub:
1. Go to your repo → **Insights** → **Network** — see the branch/merge graph
2. Click **Pull requests** → **Closed** — see your merged PR
3. Click **Commits** — see the full history

Your final repo should have:
- [ ] At least 6 meaningful commits
- [ ] Evidence of branching and merging in the graph
- [ ] 1 merged Pull Request
- [ ] Clean main branch (no unmerged branches)
- [ ] Proper `.gitignore`

**Submit:** Your GitHub repo URL showing commit history, branch graph, and merged PR.

expected_output: A GitHub repository with meaningful commit history, at least 2 branches, a resolved merge conflict, and a merged Pull Request — demonstrating the full Git workflow
